claims.text: Rainier Avenue South & Letitia Avenue South had 41 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 0 people killed.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $2.8 million a year.
12% of crashes here were recorded as “motor vehicle ran off road - hit fixed object” crashes, against 5% at the city's worst crash locations.

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: passed the causal gate (pedestrian injury crashes changed -33% (95% interval -52% to -13%) at 371 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing); a second run of the same design on 366 sites agrees.
Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons would avoid about 0.7 crashes a year (CMF 9024, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: the record FHWA cites), worth $227,000 a year.
Pavement Friction Management would avoid about 0.8 crashes a year (CMF 195, the only eligible record; evidence: national studies only), worth $289,000 a year.
The Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) is responsible for Rainier Avenue South (no route reference, so presumed a city street).
A request letter to the Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) is ready to draft from these facts.
